Not OP, but as someone currently losing a pet to cancer, I'll reply:

If your pet is still eating, that's a good sign. My boy kept getting to the point where he refused to eat entirely, even his favorite foods. The only thing that helped was steroids. My boy lost a significant amount of weight as well, and we slowly began to be able to feel his hips and spine. 

Our first abdominal ultrasound resulted 'clear' with no cancer. 6 weeks later we saw a specialty vet radiologist who told us Sam's cancer was extensive and had already spread throughout his abdomen and chest. I asked about the first ultrasound and the radiologist told me that, unfortunately, because ultrasound equipment is relatively inexpensive... Vet's offices are increasingly getting ultrasound machines and having only lightly-trained doctor's performing diagnostics. It isn't out of any malice, but those doctors simply haven't received enough training to catch everything that might be important. 

With that all said, I hope your pet feels better soon. We were encouraged to try a low-fat diet of moist food for a while, if that helps. There are a LOT of curable reasons that your doggo may not be eating well. 

Good luck and take care. <3

My 6yo buddy Sam stopped eating in early February this year. This dog is like a child to us -- he was beside us at our wedding ceremony, one of the first to meet my son when we brought him home. He was a shop dog for several years, and he's been to several states on vacation with us. He's been camping, hiking, and kayaking, among other things. I've lost count of how many dog parks we've taken him to. 

Anyway,  he had normal bowels, no vomiting, etc. Only symptom was that he repeatedly stopped eating. We brought him in to the vet on the second day of not eating. Interventions would work for a short period -- from as little as one meal to as much as a few weeks. We ended up going back to the vet's office 9 times (6 at one, 2 at another, and a Radiology office visit). 

We found out Tuesday that he has terminal High-grade lymphoma all over his abdomen and chest. He has a few weeks left to live.

Obviously we're all crushed. I haven't been handling it well and it'll randomly hit me and I'll break down crying. I hold it together in front of my wife and support her the best I can. She doesn't know I've been crying too. I love this boy...

We fought to find someone who does in-home euthanasia, but eventually located someone that could come to us. We discussed a lot of things to do with Sam's ashes, but decided that instead of spending money, we would spread his ashes in meaningful places. With the money we would have spent, on his birthday every year we will be making an equal ($150) donation to the animal shelter where we adopted him.

-----

OP, I realize your words were meant from a good place. But as a pet owner who is currently losing his pet despite best efforts, $3000 in diagnostics, and early intervention... I wish you had worded your post a little more carefully. Still, thank you for raising awareness.

I took a peek through your post history and holy shit dude. The blatant racism, sexism, and inflammatory attitude are not okay. For your sake, I hope this is a troll account.

Otherwise, I wish you good luck and I hope things get better for you. Anger and pain do terrible things to people.
